editorial:
He Who Gets Slapped (1924) was the first film released by the newly formed Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer, directed by Swedish filmmaker Victor SjÃ¶strÃ¶m (credited as Victor Seastrom) and starring Lon Chaney as a humiliated scientist who reinvents himself as a circus clown. Adapted from Leonid Andreyev's 1914 Russian play, the film paired Chaney's physical performance with early work from Norma Shearer and John Gilbert, earning MGM immediate prestige. For today's creators, it offers SjÃ¶strÃ¶m's assured direction, Chaney at his most expressive, and genuine historical weight as a studio's debut release â€” all at the image level without restriction.

The print is unconditionally public domain in the US: published in 1924, it passed the applicable term-expiry threshold and became freely usable on January 1, 2020. The practical trap is accompaniment. Flicker Alley's 2024 Blu-ray restoration â€” produced by Blackhawk Films from a first-generation 35mm safety print â€” includes two separately commissioned and fully protected audio works: a piano score by Antonio Coppola and an Alloy Orchestra orchestral recording from 2013. Reproducing either audio track without a license is infringement even though the images beneath them are free. Use a silent Archive.org upload if you need footage without those strings attached.
faq: Is He Who Gets Slapped public domain?

The film print is public domain in the US â€” published in 1924, it entered the public domain on January 1, 2020 by expiry of the 95-year copyright term. The underlying Andreyev play (1914) is also public domain. What is not free: any modern musical score attached to a copy. The Flicker Alley 2024 Blu-ray carries two protected scores (Coppola piano; Alloy Orchestra orchestral), and those audio tracks cannot be used without a license regardless of the film's own status.
